motivation: Actual baseline masked BinaryRef releases its input owner while native bytes remain pending on Windows and WSL. A copied input release and whole-stream Drain are insufficient independent QoS0 write-prefix evidence.
contract: Owning-worker optional epoch, no allocation/per-write watch. Native Produced/Completed are TCP bytes, ciphertext for WSS, not payload bytes or peer acknowledgement. A successful Staged snapshot still exposes Completed for previously saved cuts; Produced excludes local unsent WSS suffixes and is not a new full-message cut until Staged clears. Later output does not extend an existing cut. Async submissions first require successful native write results. Native batch completion may be coarse. Close/abort/overflow/binding replacement invalidate success comparisons; all non-OK outputs are unchanged.
ownership: Observer uses the existing event Data/owner/code lifetime. Coalesced deferred notification outside Send/native completion, permanent epoch through observer removal. Active opaque observers refuse owned-graph admission. Native owner/hooks and existing deferred WS drive retain actual duties; terminal state clears callbacks before context retirement.

additional_checks.baseline_probes: Retained separately, not counted as candidate qualification

resource_accounting.scope: Selected WS private fields +24 bytes per instance even if inactive; existing TCP hook +16 where not already selected, existing TLS progress +24 similarly. New public checked view32, existing config128/events80 unchanged on these x64 builds. Existing Native/TLS/masking/allocator costs remain real.
resource_accounting.heap: Actual budget1 activation/query and10000 warmed successful snapshots cause no XRT allocation/refusal. This does not claim process-wide or end-to-end zero cost.

windows.scope: Single-owner warmed query loop, one million calls per sample, five samples, includes wrapper validation. Unpinned shared host. Not wire throughput, per-write hook CPU, queue-inclusive tails, equivalent-workload overhead or performance acceptance.

wsl.scope: Single-owner warmed query loop, one million calls per sample, five samples, includes wrapper validation. Unpinned shared host. Not wire throughput, per-write hook CPU, queue-inclusive tails, equivalent-workload overhead or performance acceptance.

distribution.note: Both new public functions export; new private helper does not. Five existing Core detail exports are retained. An initial overbroad no-__xrt assertion was a harness assumption, not a newly introduced export leak.
